g.data-note: The great tree in the Party Field, strung with bunting for the next birthday feast.
The finest smial on the Hill, dug in under the old oak above a garden full of flowers.
Smaller smials dug into the lower slope; their lamps go on as the day ends.
The miller's wheel dips into the Water and turns the stones that grind the Shire's flour.
An old stone bridge where the lane from the Hill crosses the Water.
